promptHtml: A learner believed the Arty's clock ran at 50 MHz, and wrote this constraints file for tick_led to say so. Fill in the period that describes a 50 MHz clock.
explanationHtml: A period is one second divided by the frequency: 1 ÷ 50,000,000 s is 20 ns, so the line says -period 20.00. It describes a clock the board does not have; the board's oscillator runs at 100 MHz, a period of 10.00, whatever the file says.

promptHtml: tick_led_noclock is level 4's tick_led built with its create_clock line left out. Below is one of the checks at the start of its timing summary.
explanationHtml: 28: the clock pins of tick_led's 28 flip-flops, 27 for the count and one for led. Vivado can see that clk drives them, but with no create_clock it has no period, so it checks no path between them. The build still finishes, and the timing summary says there are no timing constraints at all.
excerpt: There are 28 register/latch pins with no clock driven by root clock pin: clk (HIGH)
ask: How many register pins does the report say have no clock?

promptHtml: Put in order what Vivado does, during a build, with tick_led.xdc's create_clock line.
explanationHtml: The period comes first: without it there is nothing to check against. Then each path between flip-flops is found and its delays added up, and only then can a path be compared with the period. WNS, the smallest margin over every path, can be known only once all of them are compared.
steps: It reads `create_clock`: the clock on `clk` has a period of 10 ns.
It finds every path from one flip-flop to the next.
It adds up the delays of each path's cells and wires.
It compares each path with the 10 ns between rising edges.
Its timing summary gives the smallest time to spare as WNS.

promptHtml: tick_led_20ns is tick_led built with create_clock -period 20.00, though the board's clock runs at 100 MHz. Below is its Design Timing Summary.
explanationHtml: 15.036 ns to spare, and every constraint met, but measured against 20 ns, the clock the file describes. On the board, edges come every 10 ns, so each path has about 10 ns less: tick_led's own build, at 10 ns, has a WNS of 5.380. A summary is only as true as the create_clock line it was checked against.
excerpt: WNS(ns)      TNS(ns)  TNS Failing Endpoints  TNS Total Endpoints      WHS(ns)      THS(ns)  THS Failing Endpoints  THS Total Endpoints     WPWS(ns)     TPWS(ns)  TPWS Failing Endpoints  TPWS Total Endpoints
All user specified timing constraints are met.
ask: What WNS does the report give, in nanoseconds?

promptHtml: tick_led_20ns is tick_led built with a constraints file that says -period 20.00. Below is the Clock Summary from its timing summary.
explanationHtml: 50 MHz, the frequency of a 20 ns period. The Clock Summary repeats what create_clock said, so it is the place to check that Vivado timed the clock the board really has: for the Arty, 10 ns and 100 MHz.
ask: At what frequency, in MHz, did Vivado check this design?
